findings.reason: a node implementing the contour observed side lands on the plateau by construction, so it either fails a correct implementation or passes only because the shared bias is smaller than the tolerance by accident.
findings.text: §3 orders the observed side to reproduce the certificate's exact beta_p + l_i/2 "to within the certificate's own error at the production contour sampling", but the certificate's own error is its unresolved plateau: `limit` is 0.22299 at grid 161 while `analytic_route_value` sits 0.27808 above `exact` at grid 401 (`docs/figures/constraint-augmented-newton-krylov/shafranov-integral/receipt.json`), so the certificate's own exact-field contour route already misses `exact` by 0.223-0.278 — the tolerance is as large as the bias it must discriminate against, and at the 401 grid the certificate's own route would fail it

findings.reason: without naming which of the two certificate values the observed side must match, the gate has no defined pass condition and two readings of the same sentence give opposite verdicts on a correct implementation.
findings.text: §3 names "the certificate's exact beta_p + l_i/2" as the independent reference, but the receipt carries two references — `exact` (1.2325543621162165, the volume-side definition) and `analytic_route_value` (1.5106369718687442, the exact-field contour side) — and an observed side built on the contour integral of the grid-imaged field converges to the analytic *route* value, not to `exact`; the section does not say which is meant or which quantity the observed side is expected to land on

findings.reason: the done-when turns a measured control into a hard-coded expectation whose provenance the plan does not hold, so a passing implementation can fail on the number alone.
findings.text: §1's new live-counter clause asserts the build count is "76 on the MAST row", but no committed record in the tree sources that number: no kernel counter exists (`grep` finds none in `nova/`), the current reuse test counts the fixture's own nine constructions (`tests/test_equilibrium_forward_operator.py:240,242`), and the plan itself says the only driver carrying it is uncommitted — so a node cannot check 76 before it implements, and a correct builder whose block count differs fails the gate on a constant unrelated to the reuse property
